evidence: The MoF6, MoCl5, Mo(CO)6 and H2S were chosen as the Mo and S precursors, respectively. The MoF6, Mo(CO)6 and H2S were kept at room temperature (25 °C) while MoCl5 was kept at 80 °C. The vapor pressure of MoF6 was finely controlled by a metering valve and H2S by a mass flow controller (MFC) of approximately 3 sccm. The 2D MoS2 atomic layers were then fabricated using MoF6 and MoCl5 at 700 °C by ALD as follows: Both MoF6 and MoCl5 precursor exposure for 4 s, 5 s Ar purging, 3 s H2S exposure, and 5 s Ar purging. The working pressure in the furnace was maintained at approximately 2 Torr. For the Mo(CO)6 precursor, precursor exposure (Mo(CO)6) without carrier gas for 2 s, 10 sccm Ar purging for 15 s, 2 sccm H2S reactant for 5 s, and the growth temperature was 400 °C. WCl6 and diethyl selenide (DESe) were used as the precursor and reactant, respectively. A canister containing the precursor was heated to 85 °C to ensure an adequate vapor pressure and Ar was used as the carrier gas. H2 gas was injected along with DESe during the reactant time to assist the reduction of WCl6 and the removal of Cl as a form of HCl. The ALD procedure was conducted as follows: precursor exposure (WCl6) for 4 s, Ar purge for 5 s, DESe and H2 exposure for 3 s, and a final 5 s Ar purge. MoS2 was synthesized on SiO2 (285 nm)/Si substrates using MoCl5 and dimethyl sulphide (DMS) at a growth temperature of 700 °C. The bubbler containing the precursor was heated to 80 °C to achieve adequate vapor pressure and 3 sccm Ar was used for the carrier gas. The DMS and H2 flow were fixed at 20 sccm and 10 sccm, respectively. The amount of 10 mg of NaCl was added to the CVD reactor furnace, whose temperature was at 700 °C. The growth time was 15 min for the 3-layer MoS2.
